approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES language prior from an unlabeled molecular corpus and initializes a fresh policy from that frozen prior for each objective. It trains on the highest-scoring half of the new accepted batch together with the strongest eligible examples from a memory of thirty-two earlier elites. Each example retains its original accepted string and reward. Historical examples used more often receive smaller relative coefficients, while current and historical groups keep their count-based shares. The target is frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, capped individually at zero. Bounded clipped Adam updates fit squared target residuals and retain the final iterate. The policy directly samples complete SMILES, and validation and canonical novelty checks refill the announced batch.
approach.novelty: Remove repeated historical examples from the active loss and train only on the current batch elites, with their original target ceilings and a plain mean reduction. Retain the historical selection and forwarding work as passive diagnostics so the removed contribution can be measured under the same tensor shapes and random draws. Earlier siblings changed which history was replayed, its relative influence, or its target construction. The recent score-priority removal kept replay active and lowered the final score in every seed. The original current-only root used uncapped targets and supplies only one paired screening seed. This probe directly tests replay learning in the developed learner. Its activation claim is zero historical loss contribution and a changed learning direction; its utility prediction is that removing repeated access to stronger accepted history lowers the final endpoint.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-c2ef5c1d5a78 has complete summary.json and run.log pairs with macro mean 0.5227052024221274 and population SD 0.02007213966556548. Historical replay still receives half the loss coefficient mass in every history-bearing update, but its continuing contribution after target-ceiling projection has not been isolated by a complete current-only comparison. A read-only audit of the actual fifteen logs reconstructs 450 updates, including 420 history-bearing updates followed by proposals, 15 history-free initialization updates and 15 terminal updates. All 420 prospective history updates have nonzero weighted historical gradients and persisted direct combined-versus-current gradient direction differences. Their 2100 historical appearances have mean accepted reward 0.36029244018251794, or 0.3622578653702398 under the within-history coefficients, versus current mean 0.29910228164370567. History has the higher mean reward in 373 updates. Mean starting historical gradient norm is 42.829642618726616 versus 529.0762702547366 for current elites; mean combined/current cosine is 0.982777825935638. Thus history contributes stronger accepted labels but a smaller, already-practiced residual signal. Historical weighted fitting error averages 3.365615922817683 before and 2.4363433201331643 after an update, while current error changes from 50.505835358479196 to 3.531706322308275. These observations establish contribution, not necessity or protection from forgetting. The audit records 6645 passing saved-record checks at runs/SPIRAL2/policy/passive_audits/r0013-07-improve-L03/historical_contribution_audit.json; it invokes no model, optimizer, sampler or oracle and claims no saved full gradient vectors. The original replay addition n-15499bde2e65 has only one paired comparison with current-only n-4552e16d798a. The newer score-priority removal n-add5406f59a1 loses 0.02340311086556866 in paired mean while retaining replay; it shows the value of which history is selected, not the necessity of replay itself. Excess historical weighting in n-95c3f5710341 also lost score, so useful contribution cannot be inferred from greater historical influence alone.
hypothesis: Remove historical replay from the active optimization loss, fitting only the unchanged current accepted elites to their individually ceiling-projected targets with a plain mean squared residual, while retaining historical memory, selection and exposure bookkeeping solely as passive comparison state.

finding_summary.headline: Replay removal lowered final scores despite higher recorded AUC and fewer duplicate draws.
finding_summary.insights:
The developed learner still benefits from repeatedly fitting accepted history at the final endpoint. The parent's small historical gradients were not evidence that history was redundant: the records were already well fitted under continued replay. Once replay stopped, previously accepted examples often became much worse fitted even though current elites remained easy to fit. Matched initialization, exact loss isolation and the complete paired score panel support a contribution from replay in this composition. They do not show universal protection against forgetting, and the improved seed plus higher AUC leave the timing and task dependence of that contribution open.

The result separates useful search from generic novelty. Deco-hop explored more distinct nonempty molecular cores, 438 versus 355, yet finished worse. The supplied chemistry assessment finds familiar aromatic amide, sulfonamide and cyclic-amine families on both sides; generally smaller molecules and broad ring coverage did not reliably recover the stronger parent's fragment arrangements. New molecules shared a core with the selected historical set in 320 of 4,200 subsequent emissions, versus 685 with active replay, but that association cannot identify which remembered molecule caused a score change. Unspecified stereochemistry, oversized outliers and unstable-looking linker alternatives remain unresolved.

This removes historical loss contributions, not learned historical information: policy parameters and persistent Adam moments retain earlier current learning. Passive memory selection, exposure counts and union forwarding also remain, so fewer duplicate draws do not establish a replay runtime saving. Individual target ceilings remain active but do not make the joint current target set attainable: 177 of 420 nonterminal current sets still demand total sequence probability above one. Further contribution tests must keep those residual target constraints and the difference between early AUC and final quality explicit.
finding_summary.results:
Historical examples received exactly zero loss weight and zero likelihood derivatives in all 5,220 real optimizer steps containing history. All 420 history-bearing updates followed by proposals changed the gradient direction after clipping; every real first backward matched the current-only objective exactly. All fifteen matched initialization controls reproduced the same first twenty accepted records, and every session completed its budget.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.495640, a paired decrease of 0.027066, exceeding the registered 0.002 effect. Seed changes were +0.008523, -0.023353 and -0.066368; population score dispersion fell from 0.020072 to 0.011865. Every task mean fell, led by sitagliptin (-0.072443) and deco-hop (-0.041088), then median (-0.015291), zaleplon (-0.006499) and docking (-0.0000068). Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.405593 to 0.430068, with docking reaching strong scores earlier. The final-score loss therefore coexists with better discovery earlier in the recorded budget.

Current projected fitting error fell from 60.166 to 3.804 within updates. On the same actual updates, weighted error on passively observed history rose from 69.678 to 86.195; under active replay in the parent it fell from 3.366 to 2.436. Those are fitting measurements on each run's own states. Raw duplicate draws fell from 32.21% to 25.99%, and batches needing extra sampling fell from sixteen to three, while raw validity fell from 91.79% to 87.35%.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, sulfonamides and cyclic amines dominate, with oversized outliers and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied child and parent trajectories were read, and every requested task is covered. Each task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure-token rates range from 0.9759 to 0.9966, aromatic-token rates from 0.9368 to 0.9943, and mean SMILES lengths from 37.8 to 47.6. These counters measure presence in molecular strings, not fractions of aromatic atoms or practical feasibility. The output spans ordinary aromatic amides, sulfonamides, aza-heterocycles, indoles, piperazines, piperidines, hydrazones and some larger natural-product-like or lipid-like structures. Leading families are generally recognizable synthetic chemistry, with ordinary sulfur functional groups and carbon-bound halogens. Structural diversity is broad across and within seeds, though local high-score excerpts often concentrate on related cores. Typical molecular sizes are comparable to or smaller than parent n-c2ef5c1d5a78, while occasional very long chains and large ring systems remain. The charged-token rates of 0.0391-0.0989 include nitro, azide and N-oxide representations; they do not by themselves demonstrate alternative protonation states of basic amines. Every stereocentre-token rate is 0.0. Plausible synthesis here means that most leading structures use familiar fragments and linkages, not that routes or stable stereoisomers were demonstrated. Size and configuration counts below are passive RDKit readings of supplied SMILES. Score comparisons are confined to observed molecules and do not establish target binding, an unseen required scaffold or a causal effect for changes that alter several features.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 23 heavy atoms, with a range of 7-48. Leading molecules are compact fused aza-aromatics or indoles attached to an amide or ketone and another aryl group. The highest observed molecule has 24 heavy atoms: a fused diaza-aromatic carboxamide acylates an aryl-substituted pyrrolidine, whose phenyl group carries a phenol. Its cyclic amide nitrogen is not a free aliphatic amine. Other leaders include quinoline-like carboxanilides, a dimethylamino benzofused diazinone with a benzoyl group, and indole amides containing small imine/N-N rings. These are mostly conventional medicinal fragments, although the small imine rings need closer feasibility scrutiny. Low molecules include extremely long alkyl-linked polyamines, bulky multiaryl structures and enlarged heterocycles with several appended amides; size and flexibility become much less controlled.
liabilities: Long hydrocarbon segments, repeated aryl groups and multiple appended amides produce excessive size or flexibility in the low-score tail.
Small imine-containing N-N rings and unsaturated linkers are less routine than the ordinary amide series.
The leading arylpyrrolidine has an unassigned tetrahedral centre.
missing_features: The oversized low-score products lack the compact heteroaromatic/carbonyl organization retained by the stronger structures.

The hydroxyl-free analogue lacks the phenolic group associated with the strongest local example; positional changes show that simply adding a heteroatom is not equivalent to reproducing its arrangement.
The substituted pyrrolidine configuration is unspecified, and the small imine/N-N ring alternatives do not establish a complete set of stable, geometrically defined linkers.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The phenolic arylpyrrolidine amide scores 0.5 versus 0.4519753205796759 for its corresponding phenyl analogue without the hydroxyl group. A different hydroxyl-regioisomer bearing fluorine scores 0.4603736522870685; both position and substitution differ, so this is not a fluorine-only comparison. The dimethylamino benzofused diazinone/ketone scores 0.471981152610369, while converting that dimethylamino substituent into a dimethylamide gives 0.44989726212142783. By contrast, the long polyamine reaches 0.0, and a large, highly aromatic branched derivative scores 3.23625721744337e-34. The observed preference is for compact and specifically positioned aromatic/polar functionality rather than extra rings or appended amines. Relative to the parent, seed 0 changes from an indole amide maximum of 0.43351949803907636 to the phenolic cyclic amide at 0.5. Seeds 1 and 2 move to different leading families with maxima 0.4187728703049131 and 0.471981152610369, versus parental 0.4767312946227961 and 0.5.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 28 heavy atoms, compared with 33 in the parent, although current outliers span 4-99. Leading examples are substituted heteroaryl assemblies: an anilino fused diazine joined to thiazole and malondiamide, an anilino pyridine relative, and a substituted triazine carrying pyridyl nitrile and aryl groups. Other families contain polyaryl ethers, N-N aza-heterocycles, or fused N-H heterocycles bearing aryl carboxamides. Most are synthetically recognizable, but aromatic surface and substitution can be extensive: a polyaryl-ether leader has 42 heavy atoms, and another strong example has 53 heavy atoms with a long amide/polyamine side chain. Nitro groups, a pyridine N-oxide and a heterocyclic thione occur in later molecules. Low examples include tiny halocarbons and an aromatic nitrile-substituted alkenyl sulfone/thione compound.
liabilities: Many aromatic rings and long appended amide/polyamine chains can complicate solubility, conformation and synthesis even with ordinary valence.
Nitro, N-oxide and thione chemistry introduces distinct redox or tautomeric considerations; these charged representations should not be confused with protonated amines.
The low-score alkenyl sulfone bearing a nitrile has an electrophilic unsaturated motif.
missing_features: The small low-score fragments lack the connected heteroaryl/aryl and donor-acceptor architecture of stronger molecules; the low aromatic sulfone also shows that possessing those atom types without the right connectivity is insufficient.

A compact, complete set of matched linker and substituent alternatives around the stronger heteroaryl assemblies is not demonstrated. The tied peripheral variants do not show a requirement for their particular fluorinated side chains.
The large polyaryl and polyamine examples do not supply evidence that their extra size or conformational freedom is necessary.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The anilino fused-diazine/thiazole/malondiamide structure scores 0.5970617559087443, its pyridine-containing relative 0.5930306905370843, and the decorated triazine 0.5904510410975536. The nitrile-bearing alkenyl sulfone/thione structure scores only 0.29576032540675845 despite substantial aromatic and nitrogen content, while tiny halocarbons remain near 0.5. Thus neither ring count nor generic chemical complexity explains the gradient. Three nitro/aza-heterocyclic analogues share exactly 0.5845887135341942 with quite different fluoroalkoxy or carbamate appendages, showing that those peripheral changes are not distinguished here. The parent retains more substituted azine-rich leading families. Current per-seed maxima are 0.586764705882353, 0.5970617559087443 and 0.5860900982273908, versus parental 0.5998615059406662, 0.6263699396108253 and 0.6669492630755185. The generally smaller current molecules do not reproduce the parent best fragment arrangements.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 26 heavy atoms, and the displayed leaders contain 23-29. They combine substantial aryl surface with accessible aliphatic amines. One family is a propyl-substituted indole bearing a dichlorophenyl group and a bridged bicyclic diamine. Another is a methyl/aryl-substituted piperidine with a long arylalkyl N-substituent. Other leaders combine aminotetralin/thiazole/pyrrolidine fragments, or phenolic benzylamine, piperidine and a fused aryl ether. These are plausible medicinal scaffolds with ordinary bonding, although the chlorinated aryl groups, long chains and several basic centres can make physicochemical behavior demanding. The lowest molecules instead contain aromatic imides, amides, sulfonamides or acylhydrazones, often with nitro substituents and without the same accessible aliphatic-amine arrangement.
liabilities: Long arylalkyl chains and multiple chlorinated aromatic groups add hydrophobic surface and flexibility.
Several potentially basic centres coexist without explicit protonation-state comparisons.
The leading bridged diamine and arylpiperidine each have two unassigned tetrahedral centres in passive RDKit readings.
missing_features: The low amide/imide/sulfonamide compounds lack the freely available aliphatic-amine and aryl-linker organization common to stronger products.
The high-scoring set does not establish a need for its longest chains or heaviest aromatic halogenation; more compact matched relatives are not systematically resolved by the near-saturated score.
The substituted piperidines, tetralin systems and bridged diamines lack specified configurations. Their neutral strings also leave actual amine protonation unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The indole/bridged-diamine structure scores 0.9999968787724475; the long arylalkyl piperidine scores 0.9999957763030985, and a smaller aminotetralin/thiazole/pyrrolidine compound scores 0.999994595195424. Aromatic nitro imide and nitro amide examples score 7.587654541827918e-06 and 7.6018444764176e-06. This associates accessible aliphatic amines together with aryl spacing with the stronger scores; aromatic surface alone is insufficient. Matched terminal aryl fluorine/chlorine variants share 0.9999872465278599, and extending propyl to butyl on the indole changes 0.9999968787724475 to 0.9999963450040522. The near-saturated scores do not establish a benefit from greater chain length or heavier halogenation. The parent also has aryl/cyclic-amine and flexible diamine leaders with scores close to 1, but different structures. The shared chemical association persists; these reported scores do not demonstrate experimental affinity or other drug properties.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 23 heavy atoms, with a range of 6-54. The stronger families are ordinary substituted piperazines, piperazinones and aryl sulfonamides, often with amide, carbamate or benzodioxole groups. The highest observed molecule has 27 heavy atoms and a piperazine capped by an aryl sulfonyl group and an aryl carbonyl group; both ring nitrogens are acylated or sulfonylated rather than freely basic. Another strong family contains a benzodioxole-benzyl substituent on a piperazinone. Simple N-methyl arylsulfonyl piperazines are already close in score. A separate seed reaches a compact fused indole/lactam framework. Low products include allyl isothiocyanate, allyl azide, long-chain charged nitrogen derivatives and simple aliphatic acid/amide fragments. The leading structures are generally synthetically plausible, with familiar polar linkers rather than exotic sulfur valence.
liabilities: Alkyl azide and isothiocyanate examples are reactive small fragments rather than complete medicinal scaffolds.
Some expanded aromatic assemblies add size and multiple polar linkers without a clear local score advantage.
The fused indole/lactam alternative has unassigned ring stereochemistry, although many piperazine leaders are achiral.
missing_features: The lowest small or long-chain fragments lack the linked aromatic, cyclic-nitrogen and polar-linker arrangement found in stronger structures.
The current leading excerpt does not recover the full aryl/heteroaryl and sulfonyl arrangement of the strongest parent family, despite substantial access to piperazines and sulfonamides.
There is no demonstrated need for much of the added aromatic bulk: a compact conventional sulfonamide already sits near the current maximum.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The arylsulfonyl/benzoyl piperazine scores 0.2146585422450621 and the benzodioxole-containing piperazinone 0.2125118592516207. A much simpler arylsulfonyl N-methylpiperazine has 16 heavy atoms and scores 0.20718664161756667. Adding chlorine to that simple arylsulfonyl analogue gives 0.20444464181057284, so halogenation is not uniformly rewarded. Allyl isothiocyanate and allyl azide both score 0.0, while the long-chain nitrogen/acid compound scores 0.019641313778463534. The gradient favors an assembled aromatic/cyclic-nitrogen/polar-linker pattern over isolated reactive fragments or long aliphatic chains; it does not require every ring nitrogen to remain basic. The parent already has this piperazine/sulfonamide theme. Current seed 0 and seed 1 maxima are 0.2146585422450621 and 0.2125118592516207, versus parental 0.2125118592516207 and 0.20428349275442803. Current seed 2 instead reaches an indole/lactam at 0.2026197589927496, below the parent bis-arylsulfonyl piperazine at 0.2588686674995393.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 24 heavy atoms, with a range of 7-53. The strongest current family is a readily recognizable acylhydrazone: a methoxyphenyl imine connects through N-N and carbonyl/methylene groups to an aniline bearing a benzodioxole ring. The leading molecule has 24 heavy atoms. Other relatively strong molecules include a nitrogen-rich fused dione with thiol and trifluoromethylphenyl groups, a compact N/O ring system with an aryl sulfone, a sulfonylpiperidine/imidazole, a sulfonamidoethyl aryl ester, and acetanilide-thioether aza-heterocycles. The low-score excerpt instead contains very long lipid-like chains, large lactones, extended mixed-function chains and bulky polycyclic structures. These need not be impossible to synthesize, but they differ sharply in size and topology from the compact stronger families. The current leaders use familiar chemistry; acylhydrazone configuration, stability and tautomeric identity remain unresolved.
liabilities: The leading acylhydrazone contains an imine and N-N connection, so geometric isomerism and context-dependent hydrolytic stability deserve scrutiny.
Thiol/thione tautomerism, esters and long flexible linkers occur in other families.
Lipid-like chains and large lactones introduce substantial conformational and physicochemical differences, and highly substituted polycycles are stereochemically undefined.
missing_features: Long-chain and oversized low-score molecules lack the compact polar-group arrangement associated with the stronger current series.

The weaker methoxy/methyl and nitrogen/oxygen variants do not preserve the exact local functionality of the strongest hydrazone. Stable alternative linkers preserving its spatial polar pattern remain incompletely demonstrated.
The hydrazone double-bond geometry and possible tautomers are unspecified, as are configurations in the more constrained alternatives.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The para-methoxy acylhydrazone scores 0.25824569669903324 and its meta-methoxy regioisomer 0.25283201444535275. Replacing the para-methoxy group by methyl gives 0.21244255967196835; replacing the aniline N-linkage by an ether gives 0.2230457699092374. These comparisons associate the particular oxygen/nitrogen placement within a compact linker arrangement with stronger scores. They change composition as well as donor/acceptor properties, so a single physical cause cannot be isolated. The fluorinated fused dione scores 0.2265191441292462, while the strongest hydrazones contain no halogen; fluorination alone is not the explanation. Several long-chain and macrolactone examples score 0.0. The parent leading families are different: a guanidino aryl cyclic amine at 0.2711448282680827, a carbonyl/thiourea heterocycle at 0.26424211308214746, and an amino-acylsulfonamide with fluorinated aryl substitution at 0.32609684308650033. The current hydrazone, fused dione and sulfonamido ester maxima do not reproduce those higher parent values.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A 24-heavy-atom phenolic cyclic amide scores 0.5 while a 48-heavy-atom long-chain polyamine scores 0.0. In another panel, compact 24-heavy-atom hydrazones reach 0.25824569669903324, whereas long lipid-like chains and a large lactone score 0.0. Small isolated reactive fragments also fail to reproduce the stronger assembled scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently maintain compact, coherent fragment assemblies while exploring size and topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make bounded linker, branch and ring-size alternatives available around intact useful fragment arrangements. Include coherent contractions and expansions rather than relying on either severe fragmentation or long-chain extension to explore new structures.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Matched aryl fluorine/chlorine variants share 0.9999872465278599. Extending an indole propyl group to butyl changes 0.9999968787724475 to 0.9999963450040522. A 16-heavy-atom arylsulfonyl piperazine scores 0.20718664161756667, near the more elaborate current 0.2146585422450621 maximum; adding chlorine to the simple analogue gives 0.20444464181057284.
transferable_gaps.gap: Added chain length, aromatic bulk and halogenation are not reliably coupled to useful chemical changes in the output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide matched simpler and less heavily substituted alternatives that preserve the main ring and polar-group arrangement. Let observed feedback distinguish useful additions from chemically costly appendages, without assuming that greater size or heavier halogens are beneficial.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A phenolic cyclic amide scores 0.5 versus 0.4519753205796759 without its hydroxyl group. A methoxy acylhydrazone scores 0.25824569669903324, versus 0.21244255967196835 for the methyl relative and 0.2230457699092374 for the nitrogen-to-oxygen linker replacement. Merely retaining rings and a similar number of heteroatoms does not reproduce these arrangements.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently preserve the placement of useful donors, acceptors and polar linkers across related molecular frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support controlled positional-isomer and linker comparisons that change one local chemical role while preserving the rest of the attachment framework. Extend that coverage to stable alternatives for imine/N-N linkers and small strained heterocycles, rather than treating all heteroatom replacements as equivalent.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every stereocentre-token rate is 0.0. Leading substituted piperidines and bridged diamines have two unassigned tetrahedral centres, the phenolic pyrrolidine has one, and the acylhydrazones omit imine geometry. Charged digest examples include nitro, azide and N-oxide groups; the leading aliphatic amines are represented neutrally.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not define stereochemistry and relevant molecular states for otherwise plausible medicinal scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and specify feasible stereochemical relationships and double-bond geometry when constructing substituted rings or imine linkers. Represent or track chemically plausible protonation and tautomer alternatives where appropriate, so a charge-bearing functional group is not mistaken for exploration of an amine protonation state.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

branches: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
retained_mechanisms: Unlabeled corpus next-token training of a recurrent autoregressive SMILES prior with fixed-holdout checkpoint selection.
Fresh independent objective policy and Adam state initialized from a checkpoint-verified frozen prior.

Current accepted-batch top-half elites fitted to frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times original accepted reward, with individual positive targets capped at zero and nonpositive targets preserved.
Active current-only mean squared residual with five equal current coefficients, exactly zero historical coefficients and original accepted serialization provenance.
Persistent bounded Adam, norm-one gradient clipping, inherited stopping threshold and final-iterate retention.
Direct complete autoregressive policy sampling, RDKit validation, canonical novelty filtering and bounded direct-policy refill.
Task-local canonical top-32 accepted-elite memory and descending-score historical selection retained only for passive comparison and unchanged union tensor context.
